title: Write Facts the Way Models Read Them: Lifting the Two-Hop Curse
abstract: arXiv:2611.01519v2 Announce Type: new  Abstract: A language model that learns a new fact by fine-tuning can repeat it but cannot reason with it: taught that a person is a citizen of a new country, it still cannot say, without chain-of-thought, who the head of state of that person's country is. This two-hop curse is widely treated as a reasoning deficit, and the strongest knowledge editors answer it with synthesized reasoning data. We show that the reasoning is intact and the writing is wrong. Fine-tuning writes a new fact as an answer to be said, whereas the second hop reads the bridge ("that person's country") as an entity, from the middle layers on: patching the model's own representation of the entity into the bridge at those layers largely restores the second hop, yet after fine-tuning the bridge there is no closer to the new entity than before the edit. We therefore propose read-equivalent writing (Legible): one loss term makes the bridge phrase, at the layer where the second hop

translated_title: 以模型读取的方式书写事实：破解两跳诅咒
translated_abstract: arXiv:2611.01519v2 公告类型：新 摘要：通过微调学习新事实的语言模型能够复述该事实，却无法用它进行推理：教会模型某个人是新国家公民之后，它仍然无法在不借助思维链的情况下说出这个人所在国家的国家元首是谁。这种“两跳诅咒”通常被视为推理能力缺陷，而最强的知识编辑方法则通过合成推理数据来解决它。我们证明：推理能力是完好的，错的是事实的书写方式。微调把新事实写成一个“要说出口的答案”，而第二跳推理从中间层开始就把桥接短语（“那个人的国家”）当作实体来读取：在相应层将模型自身对该实体的表征修补进桥接短语，可以基本恢复第二跳推理；然而微调之后，桥接短语与该新实体的接近程度并不比编辑前更高。因此我们提出“读取等价书写”（Legible）：用一个损失项让桥接短语在第二跳读取它的那一层（摘要在此处截断）
tldr: 论文发现两跳推理失败并非推理能力缺陷，而是微调把新事实写成了“答案”导致桥接短语缺乏实体表征，据此提出“读取等价书写”（Legible），用单一损失项使事实的写入方式与模型读取桥接实体的方式对齐，从而破解两跳诅咒。
en_tdlr: The paper shows that the two-hop curse stems not from a reasoning deficit but from fine-tuning writing new facts as answers rather than as bridge-entity representations, and proposes read-equivalent writing (Legible), a single loss term that aligns how facts are written with how models read the bridge entity, thereby lifting the curse.
